page.overview:
Who is Corrin IV?

Emperor Corrin IV was Emperor of the Known Universe (r. 1701–1735 AG), the first to rule since the death of Henoor III in 1604, nearly a century prior.

Prior to his accession, Corrin IV was known as Prince Corrin bin Alman bin Henoor; he was thus the son of an Alman and the grandson of an Henoor. Corrin's family were distant heirs of House Corrino, descending from Emperor Corrin II (who ruled more than a millennium earlier, in 477–482).

After the death of the previous Corrino emperor, Henoor III, without immediate heirs in 1604, the government of the Imperium was placed under a Landsraad-led Regency to sort out various claims to the imperial throne. The Regency collapsed in 1680, when regents Maria I Mustami and (two weeks later) Damiano Fulgencio resigned due to large amounts of unrest in the Imperium. This unrest was artificially stimulated through weapon sales by Iraklii Harkonnen. After 1680, the only Imperium-wide government was a loosely organized committee of different Houses Major. Iraklii eventually rooted out Prince Corrin and promoted his accession to the throne as a solution to the Imperium's ills. The Houses Major saw this hope in the midst of the chaos as an almost divine solution and thus elected the prince as Corrin IV in 1701.

Corrin IV established a new ruling branch of House Corrino upon his accession, the First House of Corrin Corrino. One of Corrin's first acts as emperor was to reward Iraklii Harkonnen. The emperor introduced House Harkonnen as a House Major and named Iraklii as Baron Saugus, in the Colton Sector. Corrin pressed the Landsraad to confirm his actions. The Landsraad confirmed the promotions of House Harkonnen in 1717.
